question: Can any further in-field root extraction, after arbitrary products and rational rescalings of the retained dictionary, create an extra Selmer class?
gate: Normalize all generators by D(a)=a^3/Norm(a), which has norm one and the same squareclass as Norm(a)*a. Replace the unique relation generator by D(w). If the resulting 4150 generators are independent modulo squares, the enlarged group is 2-saturated. All in-field radical operations then have the same squareclass image, already excluded from adding Selmer classes by good-prime valuations.
inputs: The fixed 4134-element early norm pool, its complete ideal parity data, the sixteen generic classes, the exact sole-relation root, and the completed affine ramification obstruction. No exceptional class, point, rank label, parameter or new relation is selected.
failure: UNKNOWN if the replacement independence or exact norm-one relation fails. The exclusion concerns the entire in-field radical closure of this frozen multiplicative dictionary; it is not a full Selmer/class-group bound and excludes neither new generators nor constructions over extensions.
